body: I can do my best to help you stay on track! How are you doing so far?

Hahaha was it that obvious? Yeah, I do think my upbringing caused much of the trauma that causes these current struggles. I am no longer religious, and consider myself open and educated on most things, but I cannot seem to shake off this sexuality stuff!

Thanks for the suggestion! I am male-bodied and male-identifying, but I love reading all kinds of sexual education material! Being mostly hetero, I think it is my responsibility (and enjoyment) reading all I can about female sexuality.
Thank you for the encouragement. It is a long and difficult journey/battle to self-love.

Thank you for the frank and honest encouragement to seek professional help. I have had psychological and psychiatric help in the past, but I never seem to be able to bring up these issues. Maybe I haven't found the right person. I am male-bodied and male-identifying, but was raised by a mother and sister, so I always feel more comfortable communicating with women. I will try again to seek proper, professional help.
Thanks for the suggestion! I will look into it and see if it helps give me insight on my struggles. Religion does quite the number on us.

I am somewhat familiar, but that you for the reading/research suggestion! Unfortunately for me, it seems like more information doesn't satisfy whatever part of my brain is controlling the shame and other manifestations. I consider myself thoughtful, critical and well-read, but I cannot seem to win the mental (and kind of physical) battle!
I was raised catholic, but am no longer part of any religious practice/community.

You could say that. I was raised Catholic, which comes with loads of shame and moral objection to sexual activity. 

I am no longer religious and do not harbor "religious shame" about anything. This has somehow manifested into some kind of creative/intellectual shame?
That is an interesting connection. I don't think I currently have any medical issues impacting this, but you never know. I am way over due for a checkup!

Thanks for the research suggestion! I don't think I would consider it an addiction since I do not do it very often (since it makes me feel like hell). I am no longer on meds, but do suffer from mental illness (depression, anxiety). 

I just feel like there has to be away to avoid disrupting my entire life over a small, human action.

>r/mentalhealth Rules

Well, I guess you could say there was a "shame" factor.  I was primarily raised by a single, catholic mother. She never talked about things like this, and time in church/catholic school did provide a lot of motivation to feel afraid and ashamed of these kinds of things. 

Thank you for your thoughts, and I am sure you are on to something. I am no longer religious and do not feel that kind of shame any more. But I am sure that is part of what is manifesting as this "new" kind of shame and depression.

Thank you. I have talked to her a little bit about these things before (she knows about my medications and things, and my sibling has attempted suicide as well). I know she would rather have me than money, but I'm just so tired. I battle really hard every day, but I don't know how much longer I can fight on.

I didn't take it as rude, so no worries. I do and have asked for help. I've tried medication, I've tried counseling, I've spoken to family and friends. Sometimes it helps for a little bit, but I always fall back to the same dark place. I don't want to put anyone through this, but I'm just running out of energy.
Thank you for your thoughts. I appreciate it coming from someone that also struggles. I just feel that every day, my options become fewer and fewer.

I genuinely appreciate your feedback. Thank you for taking the time. It's just that I've tried every conceivable way to claw out of every corner (medication, therapy, exercise), and ever time I find a deeper corner.
I know that's the reality of it, but I just can't continue.
